features.name: comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly acknowledge the validity of the original post's initial premise before introducing its divergence from the OP?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly acknowledges that the OP's initial premise (the starting claim/assumption in title or argument) is valid, reasonable or correct, and (b) afterwards in that same comment introduces a point of divergence/disagreement. Both parts must be in the same comment, in that order; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Generic politeness or acknowledging only a side point does not count; the acknowledgment must be of the premise. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Return 0 if no comment qualifies or the list is valid but empty; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Title and argument are read only to identify the OP's premise.

h0: comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging has no association with the likelihood of OP view change.
h1: Discussions with comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging = 1 have a higher likelihood of OP view change.
note: Presence (at least one comment) assumed as quantity. "Initial premise" is interpreted from current title/argument text; the original pre-edit text is unavailable, and the argument may contain edits or outcome announcements. Comment order/timing is unknown. Association only, not causal.
